sources.title: JK Cement Q2FY27 result: Profit rises 6.3% to ₹169 cr; revenue jumps 23.7%
sources.description:
JK Cement Ltd on Saturday reported a 6.31 per cent increase in its consolidated net profit to Rs 169.3 crore for the September quarter of FY2026-27, helped by volume gains.
The company had posted a net profit of Rs 159.25 crore in the July-September period a year ago, according to a regulatory filing from JK Cement Ltd (JKCL), the flagship company of JK Organisation Group.
Its revenue from operations was up 23.65 per cent to Rs 3,733.42 crore in the September quarter of FY27 compared to Rs 3,019.20 crore in the year-ago period.
The company reported "robust volume growth and higher profitability despite cost pressures," JKCL said in its Investor Presentation.
Its grey cement sales volume rose 21 per cent to 5.37 million tonnes (MT) in the second quarter of FY27. Similarly, white cement volume was up 13 per cent to 0.49 MT.

sources.title: AU Small Finance Bank Q2FY27 result: Net profit jumps 53% to ₹858 crore
sources.description:
AU Small Finance Bank on Saturday reported a 53 per cent surge in net profit at Rs 858 crore for the second quarter ended September 30, 2026 on the back of improvement in interest income.
The lender had earned a net profit of Rs 561 crore in the year-ago period.
Total income rose to Rs 6,382 crore in the quarter under review from Rs 5,224 crore in the same period a year ago, AU Small Finance Bank said in a regulatory filing.
Interest income increased to Rs 5,612 crore as against Rs 4,511 crore in the corresponding second quarter of the previous year.
Net interest income of the bank improved to Rs 2,820 crore in the July-September quarter, from Rs 2,144 crore in the September quarter of 2025, registering a growth of 32 per cent.
Net interest margin increased to 5.8 per cent from 5.5 per cent at the end of September 2025.
Asset quality of the bank also improved with gross non-performing assets (NPAs) rising to 1.99 per cent of gross advances at the end of the September quarter 2026

sources.title: BPCL Q2 profit falls 22.5% to ₹4,993 cr as fuel price freeze hits earnings
sources.description:
State-owned Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) reported a 22.5 per cent fall in September quarter net profit as earnings from operations weakened due to a retail price freeze despite rising costs.
BPCL's standalone net profit declined to Rs 4,993 crore in July-September, the second quarter of fiscal 2027, from Rs 6,443 crore a year earlier, according to a company statement.
Revenue from operations rose to Rs 1.58 lakh crore from Rs 1.22 lakh crore, while Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortisation (EBITDA) fell nearly 14 per cent to Rs 9,437 crore from Rs 10,968 crore.
India's second largest fuel retailer earned USD 32.53 on turning every barrel of crude oil into fuels like petrol and diesel in July-September, as compared to USD 10.78 a barrel gross refining margin in the same period a year back.
But these gains were wiped away by losses arising from the five month old freeze in retail price revision despite a rise in cost.

sources.title: Coforge Q2 results: Net profit surges 56.5% to ₹588 cr, revenue up 53.6%
sources.description:
Coforge posted a 56.5 per cent increase in consolidated profit to Rs 588 crore in the second quarter ended September 30, 2026, driven by AI-led execution of deals, the company said on Friday.
The IT firm had posted a net profit of Rs 375.8 crore in the same period a year ago.
"Right now the margin uptake that we are seeing is in the existing fixed price projects where AI is getting infused," Coforge Chief Executive Officer and Executive Director, Sudhir Singh, said during the company's earnings call.
Coforge signed 8 large deals the highest number signed in a single quarter  across North America, Europe and Australia, which led to a total contract value of the new orders of USD 1.04 billion during the reported quarter.
The company increased the operational profit margin guidance to 17 per cent for the next year from the range of 15.5 per cent to 16 per cent.
Revenue from operations during the reported quarter increased by 53.6 per cent to Rs 6,171 crore from Rs 4,016 crore a year

sources.title: Apple India revenue grows 32% to cross ₹1 trillion mark in FY26: Tofler
sources.description:
iPhone maker Apple's India revenue grew by over 32 per cent to Rs 1,04,607 crore in FY26, according to the document shared by market intelligence firm Tofler.
The company recorded revenue of Rs 79,060.5 crore in FY25.
"Apple India Private Limited provides and markets Apple brand products and software, and reported its revenues for the financial year 2025-26 at Rs 1,04,607 crore, a 32 per cent jump since the last financial year," Tofler said.
Apple India net profit grew by 66 per cent to Rs 5,311 crore in the same fiscal.
The company's total expenses for the fiscal were reported at Rs 96,224 crore, Tofler said.
